# `compat/css-healer.js`

> **Source:** `engine/compat/css-healer.js`

css-healer.js — scope a guest app's CSS so it cannot style the OS shell. External WebGPU apps routinely style `html, body, canvas, *, :root` globally. `scopeCss(css, scope)` rewrites every style rule so it only applies inside the guest's realm container (e.g. `[data-engine-app="tempolux"]`): html, body            →  [data-engine-app="id"] canvas                →  [data-engine-app="id"] canvas *                     →  [data-engine-app="id"] * .hud .row             →  [data-engine-app="id"] .hud .row At-rules are handled correctly: @media/@supports/@container/@layer/@scope have their inner rules scoped; @keyframes/@font-face/@page/@property/@import are left intact (their "selectors" are not element selectors).

## Functions

### `scopeCss(css, scope)`

Scope a full stylesheet string to `scope` (a selector like `[data-engine-app="id"]`).

### `scopeSelectorFor(appId)`

Convenience: the canonical realm scope selector for an app id.
